entry.title: Maryland Is Getting Its Own (Mini) Sphere
entry.summary: The Prince George’s County Council has authorized up to $215 million for a venue just south of Washington, D.C.
entry.content:
East Coast concert lovers with a penchant for geodesic domes, rejoice: the Las Vegas Sphere is getting a sister venue in Maryland. WTOP reports that the Prince George’s County Council (PGCC) has approved up to $215 million in funding to build a Sphere on the Potomac River, just south of Washington, D.C.

The shape of the proposed Sphere at National Harbor will be the same, but the size will be smaller: where the Las Vegas Sphere can hold up to 20,000 people, the planned capacity for the Maryland venue is around 6,000. The new Sphere will be part of a larger complex. The PGCC voted unanimously on October 27 to push the project, which was first announced back in January, forward. Dates for both a groundbreaking ceremony and an opening have yet to be confirmed. All told, the venue is projected to cost around $1.4 billion.

“This project represents a $1.3 billion dollar economic impact to Prince George’s County and a $1.5 billion dollar impact to the state of Maryland,” County Executive Aisha Braveboy said in a news conference. “This project is projected to generate $63 million annually in just property tax and sales and amusement tax alone.” Earlier this month, the PGCC also approved a labor peace agreement that will allow Sphere workers to organize once it opens; however, this deal did not include the construction workers who will build the venue.

Since it opened in 2023, the Las Vegas Sphere has hosted large-scale residencies from U2, No Doubt, Dead & Company, Metallica, and more. Backstreet Boys, the Eagles, Carín Leon, and John Mayer all have upcoming shows slated at the venue.

Robyn opened the performance with the first verse of “Punkrocker,” giving its iconic hook a new treatment by replacing “punkrocker” with “pop star,” before transitioning into the title track of Tinashe’s recent pop manifesto.

Read more about why we love “Popstar” in Walden Green’s review.

entry.title: Xaviersobased Wants to Collab With Sabrina Carpenter
entry.summary: “Bro, I’ll knock out a whole album with her”
entry.content:
Xaviersobased has worked with OsamaSon, Lil B, and Skrillex but he has his sights set a bit higher on the Hot 100.

In a new Hypebeast cover story, the New York rapper was asked whether he would consider chart-chasing with a feature from a pop star like Sabrina Carpenter. “Bro, I’ll knock out a whole album with her,” he said. “I’m down for all types of things, but it just has to feel right and be done in a certain way.”

It’s difficult to imagine what a Xav/Sab joint would sound like—Carpenter singing something desperately horny over blown-out beats? Xaviersobased rapping over disco-pop?—but we’re here for it.

For now, revisit Alphonse Pierre’s review of the very non-Sabrina-esque Xavier.

entry.title: Jim James Announces Memoir One Wonders
entry.summary: “I hope the main thing someone takes away from this book (aside from learning more about the joys and challenges of being a working artist and musician) is that it’s okay to ask for help."
entry.content:
My Morning Jacket frontman Jim James has announced One Wonders, his first memoir, which will delve into the singer-songwriter’s upbringing in Louisville, the pitfalls of being a full-time musician, and his descent into and recovery from alcoholism and depression. It’s out April 13 on Simon & Schuster.

“If nothing else, I hope the main thing someone takes away from this book (aside from learning more about the joys and challenges of being a working artist and musician) is that it’s okay to ask for help,” James wrote in a heartfelt statement, which you can read in full below. “Everyone is going through some sort of challenge in this crazy world. IT IS POSSIBLE to find your way out of darkness and despair, and begin to enjoy the subtle, beautiful, everyday victories of simply being alive.”

In August, James premiered Wowed Out, his first solo album in eight years. He’ll be supporting it with a quick tour before the end of the year, kicking off with a hometown set in November; the full slate is listed below.

Jim James: One Wonders
$27.96 at Bookshop.org
$29 at Amazon

Hello, friends! I am releasing a memoir!

Why? Why write this book? Why now?

As I’ve made good progress in therapy over the last five or six years, I’ve been doing a lot of reflecting on finding my voice- both as a singer, songwriter and musician, and as a person wandering the earth wondering…

what do I really want to SAY with my life overall?

As I reflect on my own musical journey (from first learning to play the guitar to creating music in the present day) and navigating the complexities of life in general, I have been thinking a lot about my elders. For so many of them, tradition was to never speak about yourself. You carried your victories and failures, your joys and horrors, quietly.

A thought kept making its way into my mind: wouldn’t things be lighter for all of us if we shared more with other people?

I feel like it’s our generation’s job to tear down those walls and share our triumphs and horrors.

When we do, we’ll find that we’re all walking around with the same things inside of us, the good and the bad.

It helps so much when we can find a way to let them out together, so that we can all begin to move toward a more peaceful and love-centered existence.

As if it WANTED this to happen and was WILLING it to happen, the Universe stepped in and began to line up the things I needed to write this book, bring it to life, and ACTUALLY PUBLISH it. And I began to realize its purpose:

Perhaps if I illustrated my journey, and how I began to deal with my own struggles with mental health, it could help people take a step toward getting out of their own darkness and depression.

If nothing else, I hope the main thing someone takes away from this book (aside from learning more about the joys and challenges of being a working artist and musician) is that it’s okay to ask for help. Everyone is going through some sort of challenge in this crazy world. IT IS POSSIBLE to find your way out of darkness and despair, and begin to enjoy the subtle, beautiful, everyday victories of simply being alive.

One Wonders will be available April 13, 2027 in hardcover and ebook, and as an audiobook, which I'll be reading. Additionally, Carmichael's Bookstore in Louisville will have autographed copies that you can preorder now.

entry.title: Kevin Morby and Lonnie Holley’s New Single Raises Money for Gun Safety
entry.summary: “It is far and away the darkest and most violent song I’ve ever written”
entry.content:
Kevin Morby has shared a new Bandcamp-exclusive single called “Nursery Rhyme” featuring Lonnie Holley, with proceeds of it going toward Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in the U.S. In a statement, Morby called it “far and away the darkest and most violent song I’ve ever written,” and added he intentionally released it on Bandcamp to avoid “the risk of the song popping up in any sort of algorithm or entering someone’s psyche without permission.” Listen to the song below.

Morby originally wrote “Nursery Rhyme” in the summer of 2025. Now it arrives weeks after the fatal school shooting that took place in Bend, Oregon. “It’s hard to know what else to do in a country where the powers-that-be worship inside the church of weapons of mass destruction and value profits over the lives of our children. Sometimes you just gotta scream,” Morby added.

The song comes 10 years following the release of another Morby track about violence, “Beautiful Strangers,” which addressed the Pulse nightclub shooting and the death of Freddie Gray.

Read more about Kevin Morby in the Pitchfork feature Life & Death in Kevin Morby’s Midwest.

entry.title: Ethel Cain Made a Song for Robert Eggers’ Werwulf
entry.summary: Robert Carolan scored the gothic horror film, which hits theaters on Christmas Day
entry.content:
Remember how spooked Ethel Cain fans were when they first heard Perverts, her dark ambient album from 2025 that followed Preacher’s Daughter? It seems director Robert Eggers appreciated that atmospheric left turn from the singer-songwriter, because he’s tapped her and his former collaborator Robin Carolan to soundtrack Werwulf, his new gothic-folk horror film due out Christmas Day. The full soundtrack is out digitally December 18, with a vinyl release to follow on January 29 via Sacred Bones, but you can listen to Carolan’s title track contribution right now.

Directed by Eggers and co-written with Sjón, Werwulf puts a new spin on the classic werewolf tale, in which a 14th-century English town is haunted by a beast who threatens the safety of a man and his family. It stars Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe, and Lily-Rose Depp. Carolan wrote the bulk of the movie’s soundtrack, with Cain partnering together for the song “Wynter Waxeth.”

Describing the joint songwriting process, Carolan said: “I’d send [Cain] medieval music, prayers, weird ambient stuff, and we’d talk through it all. It was one of those rare collaborations where we just seemed to be on the same page about everything. Initially we’d talked about her contributing vocals to the score in a more textural way, but it wasn’t long until we started discussing a full blown song. Her talent and open mindedness to try different things is honestly incredible. She sang the song in Middle English, and with Rob’s help she mastered the pronunciation on the hop, practically in one session. She brought so much earthy, feral, haunted beauty to the score, and it’s hard to imagine it without her presence.”

Cain’s most recent album, Willoughby Tucker, I’ll Always Love You, came out in 2025. Meanwhile, Carolan has been steadily scoring movies for Eggers, including his 2022 viking epic The Northman and his 2024 silent horror film Nosferatu.

Revisit Madison Bloom’s interview with Carolan in How The Northman’s Composers Dreamed Up a Different Kind of Viking Movie Score.

entry.title: Panda Bear Unveils New Live Album
entry.summary: PB Band Live 25 at Power Station gathers 17 tracks cut last year at the famed New York recording studio
entry.content:
When Animal Collective’s Noah Lennox was recording Sinister Grift, his 2025 album as Panda Bear, he mostly operated as a one-man-band, playing guitar, bass, keys, and drums at different points on the LP. Given the limitations of being just one guy, touring required a different approach. Lennox recruited Tim Koh to take over bass, Maria Reis on keyboards and percussion, Tomé Silva on drums, and Spirit of the Beehive’s Rivka Ravede on samplers; all four handled backing vocals.

Now, Lennox has announced a new live album capturing the quintet in motion. The 17-track PB Band Live 25 at Power station arrives December 11 on Domino’s live studio recording series Domino Documents. The LP gathers cuts the group laid down at the famed New York studio last fall in the wake of a tour across the U.K. and Europe. The first preview, a live version of “Take Pills,” is out now. Listen below.

Since releasing Sinister Grift in 2025, Lennox has been back in his collaborative bag. He shared another joint album with Sonic Boom, A ? of When, in July, and reunited with Animal Collective for a run of live performances dedicated to their 2005 album, Feels. After initially plotting just two dates—one in New York and one in Los Angeles—the group doubled the number of shows in response to a ticketing glitch.

Read about Sinister Grift at No. 43 in The 50 Best Albums of 2025.

entry.title: Massive Attack’s Robert Del Naja Releases New Songs for Gaza Documentary
entry.summary: The Life Support soundtrack includes his new remix of Kneecap’s “Palestine”
entry.content:
Massive Attack’s Robert Del Naja has co-curated an contributed several songs and remixes to the soundtrack to a new Gaza documentary called Life Support. Out today, the soundtrack features three Del Naja originals—under his 3D alias—plus a remix of Kneecap’s “Palestine” [ft. Fawzi]. Another track, credited to the Five Techniques collective, features Paul Weller, David Holmes, and Róisín El Cherif. Listen to the whole soundtrack below. All profits from vinyl sales will go to the Health Workers 4 Palestine solidarity fund, according to a press release.

The Life Support website explains that the fim draws from the testimonies and footage from international doctors allowed into Gaza. A synopsis reads, “Covering the entire two years of the genocide, their first-hand accounts and visceral footage offer a rare and vital chronicle of the daily struggles of healthcare workers as they navigate bombed-out hospitals, dwindling supplies, starvation and the overwhelming influx of casualties—predominantly women and children.”

Other contributors to the soundtrack include Yasmine Hamdan, Habib Shehada Hanna, Massar Egbari, 47Soul, and Siba and Monkyman. The film is now streaming on demand, with dozens of screenings lined up, predominantly in the United Kingdom and Ireland, alongside Q&As with the filmmakers.

Del Naja was one of hundreds of protesters arrested in London in April for holding a placard in support of the activist group Palestine Action, which is banned under UK terrorism law.

entry.title: Everything But the Girl Ready New Album Blue Reservoir
entry.summary: Watch the “Young and Dumb” video from Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt’s Fuse follow-up
entry.content:
Everything But the Girl have lined up a new album, Blue Reservoir. After returning from a 24-year break, in 2023, with Fuse, the duo of Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt is back with 10 more originals, out February 19 via Buzzin’ Fly/Virgin Music Group. The announcement comes with new song “Young and Dumb” and a video directed by Edward Bishop from a treatment by the duo.

The video was shot at London venue Moth Club, where, last year, Thorn and Watt performed a residency that informed the direction of the new material. “There was an intensity and simplicity to the Moth shows that took us back to how we started out,” Thorn said in a press release. “Direct, rooted in guitar and voice, a few extra colors.”

Watt wrote and performed much of the album on a Spanish nylon-string guitar. “It is the sound of so much of the music I first connected with growing up, and I’d never actually owned one,” he said. “It became quite an emotional springboard for me. I found a voice I thought I’d lost.” Longtime collaborators Rex Horan and Evan Jenkins play double bass and drums, respectively, on Blue Reservoir, joined by percussionist Fabio de Oliveira.

entry.title: Hum Are Hitting the Road in 2027
entry.summary: It’s the Illinois rock band’s first proper run since 2015
entry.content:
Veteran Illinois shoegaze band Hum have announced a 2027 tour, their first proper run since 2015. The U.S. treck kicks off in Atlanta in March, stopping in Austin, Philadelphia, New York, Boston, Seattle, and more before concluding in San Francisco in July. All dates will feature support from Kansas City’s the Life and Times, while Chicago post-hardcore band Pelican and Brooklyn trio Spotlights will open on East and West Coast dates, respectively. Check out a full itinerary below.

The shows build upon Hum’s well-received headlining sets earlier this year at traveling shoegaze festival Slide Away, where they shared top billing with Chapterhouse and Nothing. Those dates were Hum’s first shows in nearly seven years, a hiatus that also encompassed the death of original drummer Bryan St. Pere in 2021. Shiner’s Jason Gerken, who joined the group on drums during their 2015 tour and at Slide Away, will return to the kit for the forthcoming dates.

Hum’s Slide Away sets marked the first time the band performed songs from their 2020 album Inlet live. Prior to that release, they hadn’t shared a record since 1997’s Downward Is Heavenward, which followed 1995’s You’d Prefer An Astronaut and their 1993 debut Electra 2000.

entry.title: Neil Young Really Wants Trump to Stop Playing “Rockin’ in the Free World”
entry.summary: He’s suing (again) over the president’s unauthorized use of the song at political rallies
entry.content:
Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Neil Young is filing suit after “Rockin’ in the Free World” was played at a Trump rally. The lawsuit—filed yesterday (Monday, October 26) in Virginia’s Eastern District Court—specifically cites an “unauthorized public performance” of Young’s 1991 protest anthem at a rally in Youngstown, Ohio on October 12. The named defendant is actually not President Donald J. Trump himself, but rather the Trump 47 Committee, his primary political action committee and the event’s organizer.

“‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ is a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless, and forgotten,” the lawsuit reads. “The lyrics paint vivid, street-level portraits—a mother discarding her baby, addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity—while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn’t shared by all. In short, the Song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for.” Pitchfork has reached out to Young’s legal representation for further comment.

Young is seeking $10 million in damages on the grounds of copyright infringement, asserting that the Trump 47 Committee did not have “license or Young’s permission” to play the song at any “purely political event.” He also demands that neither “Rockin’ in the Free World” nor any of his other songs be played at future events organized by or associated with the PAC.

During the 2020 presidential election, Young sued Trump’s campaign committee, Donald J. Trump for President Inc., over their use of “Rockin’ in the Free World” and another of his songs, “Devil’s Sidewalk,” at campaign rallies. The parties settled out of court under the stipulation, according to the new suit, that the corporation “would never use ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ without a license and permission from Young.” However, as a separate organization, the Trump 47 Committee would be exempt from the terms of that specific settlement. Agh, technicalities!

entry.title: Listen to MJ Lenderman Cover Lambchop’s “Weakened”
entry.summary: From the veteran Nashville band's new covers EP Demoed
entry.content:
MJ Lenderman has added yet another killer cover to his catalog, this time of alt-country heroes Lambchop’s song “Weakened.” The original appears on the Kurt Wagner-fronted band’s August album Punching the Clown; the new version features Lenderman singing, playing bass; and guitar alongside Fog’s Andrew Broder.

Lenderman’s take on “Weakened” appears on Lambchop’s forthcoming EP Demoed, a collection of demo covers of songs from Punching the Clown. Wagner primarily recruited younger musicians to take up the mantle, including Lauren Auder, Circuit des Yeux and Alan Sparhawk, Flock of Dimes, and More Eaze. The full EP is due November 20 digitally, and February 5 physically.

“I used to fantasize that Lambchop would continue as an idea well beyond my participation,” Wagner shared in press materials. “Over time we’ve had at least two generations represented. A third now is beginning. And this is important to me, having the unique perspective and contributions from younger artists steering in the work we make. So I thought it would be nice, someday, that I might even step aside to watch and advise from the wings. Having a beard was never considered, but here we are.”

Lenderman dropped his most recent solo album, Manning Fireweworks, in 2024. Last year, he released a live album with Karly Hartzman recorded at Nashville’s Third Man Records. Since then, he’s also released a song with This is Lorelei, and spent this past spring on tour with Waxahatchee.

entry.title: Shelved David Bowie Concert Film Revived for Immersive Live Show
entry.summary: Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen has remastered the unreleased 1978 film “Stage” for a multi-screen extravaganza
entry.content:
The unreleased David Bowie concert film “Stage”, recorded on his 1978 tour behind Low and “Heroes”, will tour arenas as a novel multimedia experience in 2027. Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen has adapted footage from Bowie’s Isolar II tour—originally shot by David Hemmings—for a multi-screen live show, also called “Stage”. It will premiere at Berlin’s Uber Arena on February 14 before further, as-yet-unannounced shows. Watch a trailer below.

Morgen originally conceived the project in 2018, while sifting Bowie’s archives for his 2022 documentary. (Hemmings’ footage of “Heroes”, the song, made the cut of Moonage Daydream.) Bowie had intended Hemmings’ film from Earls Court, in London, to play in unorthodox spaces, such as live venues, as an alternative to touring himself, The Guardian notes. In the end, Bowie released a live album, 1978’s Stage, but shelved the footage to focus on other projects; he also quit touring until 1983. “I simply didn’t like the way [Hemmings’ footage] had been shot,” Bowie told Uncut in 2001. “Now, of course, it looks pretty good and I would suspect that it would make it out some time in the future.”

Morgen spent years meticulously remastering Hemmings’ 35mm film and configuring it for multiple screens. The event will feature an integrated lighting show from Patrick Woodroffe and immersive audio mixed by Paul Massey. The elaborate LED displays and audio mix, the press release notes, are designed for “auditoriums and venues with capacities starting at 5,000, enveloping audiences in the atmosphere of a full-scale rock concert.” Rob Hallett’s Wonderworld and the David Bowie Estate also collaborated on the project.

entry.title: Factory Floor Return With First Album in 10 Years
entry.summary: Listen to “Continuation” and the title track from One Trip
entry.content:
Factory Floor, the London electronic outfit that released its buzzy debut on DFA in 2013, are back with a new album, One Trip. The double single “Continuation” / “One Trip” leads the first LP in a decade from the trio, now comprising original members Nik Colk Void and Gabe Gurnsey with new addition Joe Ward. They will bring a new live show to London Barbican, supporting Squid, on December 5. Listen to the new songs below ahead of the album release on November 27.

Factory Floor originally included Dominic Butler, who exited before second album 25 25 arrived in 2016. Gurnsey and Void continued to release music on labels such as Editions Mego and Erol Alkan’s Phantasy Sound, the latter of which is also putting out the new record following a string of recent singles.

The band returned in 2024 at Mutek Festival. After that performance, they said in a press release, “We felt an appetite to work in a space where artists could connect emotionally and physically, both in the studio and on a live stage. These environments hold more than sound; they carry a visceral energy that comes from being together. It’s something we’d really missed as solo artists, and it made us want to explore that kind of experience again.”

entry.title: Dead Man’s Bones Unveil First New Song in 17 Years
entry.summary: The duo of Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields return with “Lost in the Night”
entry.content:
After a short teaser clip lit up the internet with news of their return, Dead Man’s Bones—the duo of Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields—are officially back with their first new music in 17 years. “Lost in the Night” was produced with longtime collaborator Tim Anderson, and it gets a black-and-white music video starring Hamnet’s Noah Jupe and The Summer I Turned Pretty’s Rain Spencer that draws on its lovestruck lyrics. Check it out below.

Dead Man’s Bones set out to write new music in recent years, but couldn‘t settle on where to record it. The duo tried a number of Los Angeles studios before driving to a farm outside of the city with some gear in tow—two guitars, two drum machines, and two synthesizers—where they proceeded to record “Lost in the Night” in one day.

The first and only Dead Man’s Bones album came out in 2009. Gosling and Shields worked closely with the Silverlake Conservatory Children’s Choir, a California education organization founded by Flea, on their self-titled debut to achieve its cross of indie rock, gothic folk, and doo-wop. The duo retreated from the public eye after promoting their first album. However, they found renewed interest over the years through covers (like Cat Power tackling “Pa Pa Power” for her 2022 album Covers), various film and TV syncs, and a seasonal bump courtesy of social media users playing their music around Halloween.

Revisit Rob Mitchum’s review of Dead Man’s Bones.
